Self-audit. Round 4 added it, round 5 made it derive the changed set from git rather than from the receipt, round 6 made it survive being re-run somewhere other than this working copy. It fails when any changed path is missing from the union of the recorded G-1 and G-3 --files lists, and re-runs every recorded gate command. Every git call is now checked: a failed merge-base or diff aborts with a message instead of yielding an empty changed set and a silent all-clear. The changed set is committed diff plus tracked staged/unstaged edits; '??' untracked entries are excluded because they are not part of the branch's change until staged, and because git reports an untracked directory as a bare directory path that no --files list would ever name. Base ref is argv[1], default origin/main, for checkouts that name it differently.

greptile.note: All findings from all six rounds addressed in code on this branch. No waiver requested in any round, and none would be valid here: no instruction from Ove exists for this PR. Rounds 4, 5 and 6 found defects in this receipt rather than in the documentation, each one in the previous round's fix to it.

round_6_findings.title: Missing base yields false coverage
round_6_findings.verdict: VALID, and the more serious of the two — a false pass. The round-5 audit ignored the exit status of git merge-base and git diff. Reproduced: 'git merge-base origin/nonexistent HEAD' exits 128, base became empty, the diff yielded nothing, and on a clean tree the audit printed {'changed_paths': 0, 'uncovered': {}, 'rerun_mismatches': []} and exited 0 — reporting full G-1/G-3 coverage having checked no path at all. Third instance on this branch of a check asserting more than it verifies, after the round-1 scanner guarantee and the round-5 audit.
round_6_findings.disposition: FIXED — every git call goes through a helper that aborts with the failing command, its exit code and its first stderr line. Negative-tested: the new audit with a bad base exits 1 with "audit: 'git merge-base origin/nonexistent HEAD' failed rc=128", where the round-5 audit exited 0 on the same input.

round_6_findings.title: Untracked directories fail audit
round_6_findings.verdict: VALID — a false failure. Reproduced: with an unrelated untracked directory present, 'git status --porcelain' emits the bare directory entry '?? scratchprobe/', which the round-5 audit added to the changed set. No --files list names a directory, so it was reported uncovered and the audit failed at exit 1 even though every PR path had been checked.
round_6_findings.disposition: FIXED — '??' entries are excluded from the changed set. They are untracked, so they are not part of the branch's change until staged, and git reports an untracked directory as a bare directory path that no --files list would ever name. The changed set is now the committed diff against merge-base plus tracked staged and unstaged edits, with rename arrows resolved to the new path. Negative-tested with the same untracked directory present: the new audit exits 0 where the round-5 audit exited 1. The round-5 drift detection is retained and re-tested — an uncovered sixth file still yields uncovered={'G-1': ['docs/handoff-contracts.md'], 'G-3': [...]} and exit 1.

round_5_findings.title: Self-audit misses omitted files
round_5_findings.verdict: VALID — the round-4 audit re-ran each recorded command exactly as written, so it only ever checked the files already named. A path added to the change but never added to a --files list still passed on the shorter list, and the audit reported no mismatch. It could not detect the drift it was added to prevent, and its note asserted that it could. Same class of error as the round-1 P2 on the scanner guarantee: a claim of coverage wider than the mechanism delivers.
round_5_findings.disposition: FIXED — the audit now derives the changed set from git (merge-base diff against origin/main plus the working tree) instead of trusting the receipt, and fails when any changed path is missing from the union of the recorded G-1 and G-3 --files lists. Coverage is taken as a union across every passing recorded run of each gate, not just the first. The re-run check is kept. Negative-tested before recording: editing a sixth file without adding it to the lists yields uncovered={'G-1': ['docs/handoff-contracts.md'], 'G-3': ['docs/handoff-contracts.md']} and exit 1; reverting returns exit 0. The round-4 audit reported no mismatch for that same scenario. The claim was reworded to state what is actually checked.

round_4_findings.title: Changed document omitted from checks
round_4_findings.verdict: VALID — adding docs/cross-bot-protocol.md in round 3 made this a five-path change, but the recorded G-1 and G-3 commands still named the older three- and four-path lists. The five-path runs were executed in the working session; the receipt recorded the stale ones, so the claims citing them did not cover the added file. This is precisely the G-2 failure mode the repo exists to prevent: a claim whose cited command does not substantiate it.
round_4_findings.disposition: FIXED — commands 0, 2, 5 and 6 now name all five paths and carry their real re-run output (G-1 PASS 4 and 5 file(s), G-3 PASS 4 and 5 file(s)). The two claims were reworded from 'four changed paths' to all five, naming docs/cross-bot-protocol.md. A self-audit command was added that re-runs every recorded gate command and asserts each still matches its recorded exit code and output, so this drift cannot recur silently.

round_4_findings.title: Reproduction command cannot be rerun
round_4_findings.verdict: VALID — the round-3 reproduction recorded its cmd as a prose placeholder, '--change <change doc built from the pre-fix example>', which no reviewer could execute. An unexecutable command is not evidence.
round_4_findings.disposition: FIXED — replaced with a command that reconstructs the pre-fix document deterministically from the current tree: it reads the now-fixed example out of docs/cross-bot-protocol.md, removes the semantic_changes key, and asserts G-4 rejects it. The wrapper exits 0 when the inner G-4 run exits 1, so the entry is an assertion that the failure still reproduces rather than a recorded failure; expects_failure was dropped from the claim accordingly.

round_3_findings.title: Required contract field omitted
round_3_findings.verdict: VALID — check_contracts.py:150 requires semantic_changes outside REQUIRED_CHANGE_FIELDS, unconditionally, so it applies to non-breaking changes too; docs/handoff-contracts.md:76 states the same rule
round_3_findings.disposition: FIXED — the field list in docs/quality-gates.md now includes semantic_changes, says it is mandatory even when empty, gives the [] form and names the failure text. Greptile also noted the linked example omitted it: docs/cross-bot-protocol.md:84 was a working change document that failed the gate it documents, and whose failure message points back at that same file. Reproduced, then fixed with the key and a comment explaining why it is mandatory. The example extracted from the doc now passes G-4.

round_3_findings.title: Gate changes need human approval
round_3_findings.verdict: VALID — and corroborated inside this repo, not only in Greptile's knowledge base (docs/quality-enforcement.md is a Greptile KB document and does not exist here). prompts/QUALITY.xml:565, :729, :749 and :782 all require a human on QUALITY's own gate change, and skills/greptile-merge-gate/SKILL.md:49 repeats it. The round-2 text said 'LEAD or a human', which is too permissive for ci/gates/** and ci/hooks/**.
round_3_findings.disposition: FIXED — the sequence adds a third approver line for gate changes (a human, and only a human), and a paragraph states the rule for ci/gates/** and ci/hooks/**, cites prompts/QUALITY.xml, and says explicitly that G-2 cannot enforce it: check_receipt.py only compares the approver against the authoring bot, so a LEAD stamp on a gate change passes the gate while breaking the rule. Recorded as a policy constraint the receipt carries, not something the tooling catches.

round_2_findings.title: Contract pre-flight cannot pass
round_2_findings.verdict: VALID — reproduced: ci/gates/check_contracts.py:180 returns 1 with 'contract surfaces changed but no change document supplied' when a surface is touched and --change is absent, whether or not a change document exists on disk
round_2_findings.disposition: FIXED — the pre-flight G-4 line is annotated, the bare form is scoped to diffs touching no contract surface, and the --change form is shown with the change document's required fields and a pointer to docs/cross-bot-protocol.md and skills/contract-first-changes.

round_2_findings.title: QUALITY cannot approve itself
round_2_findings.verdict: VALID — G-2 rejects approved_by equal to the authoring bot, so bot-06 cannot stamp a change to its own files, which is exactly what this PR is
round_2_findings.disposition: FIXED — the sequence now names the approver per author (QUALITY for a build seat; LEAD or a human for QUALITY's own work, never bot-06 itself), and a paragraph gives the human:<name> and bot-00-programming-lead forms, both already in use under .receipts/bot-06-quality-security/, citing skills/verification-receipts. It also states that approved_by stays absent rather than self-filled until the independent stamp lands.

round_1_findings.title: Full pre-flight cannot pass yet
round_1_findings.verdict: VALID — confirmed against ci/gates/check_receipt.py:101, where approved_by is required unconditionally rather than only under --strict
round_1_findings.disposition: FIXED — the order-of-operations block no longer tells a seat to pass run_all.py before committing. It now names the per-gate pre-flight commands, states that G-2 is expected to fail on 'approved_by' is missing alone, and puts the first fully green run_all.py under QUALITY after the stamp.

round_1_findings.title: Scanner guarantee is overstated
round_1_findings.verdict: VALID — G-2 matches recorded command strings against the fixed BYPASS_PATTERNS list; it does not verify that a scanner was enabled or that a suite ran
round_1_findings.disposition: FIXED — the waiver section now scopes the assurance to the listed bypass forms when the command is in the receipt, and states that a command left out of the receipt is invisible to G-2, so a green G-2 is evidence about recorded commands rather than proof the right commands ran.

round_1_findings.title: Waiver policies remain inconsistent
round_1_findings.verdict: VALID — docs/github-sot-orchestration.md §4.2 describes the waiver without the explicit-Ove-instruction condition
round_1_findings.disposition: FIXED WITHIN OWNERSHIP — §4.2 is owned by bot-00-programming-lead and G-1 blocks bot-06 from editing it, so the divergence is now declared in docs/quality-gates.md: the new section is named the operative rule until LEAD reconciles §4.2, and a waiver authored against §4.2 alone does not clear a merge claim. Reconciling §4.2 remains LEAD's change.
